subject: Clarify: streaming session charges, partial outputs & retry credits
messages:

Subject: Questions on streaming billing + rate card request

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with two pricing clarifications before we take this to our legal team:

1) If a client opens a streaming generation and the model emits only a partial answer (e.g., client disconnects mid-stream, or the model times out), what gets billed?
2) If we retry a stream because of a network blip, are we charged for duplicate tokens? Any idempotency guidance or automatic crediting?
3) Can you share a short hosted-API rate card for baseline per-token and streaming-specific rules so procurement can slot it into our SOW?

We want to understand the worst-case monthly token exposure before we commit to a reserved plan.

Appreciate a compact one-pager we can circulate.

Best,
Alex
Sr. PM, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Questions on streaming billing + rate card request

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short one-pager (redwood_streaming_pricing_onepager.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan for your procurement team. Summary below; happy to jump on a quick call to walk through examples.

Short answers (high-level):
- Billing unit: we charge per-token for generated output and per-token for input (embeddings/consumed prompt) under the hosted API. Streaming is not a separate SKU — it’s the same per-token metering but delivered over a streaming response.
- Partial outputs (client disconnect or client-side abort): tokens that were emitted by the model and successfully accepted by our runtime are billed. If the client closes the socket before receiving the last bytes, the server-side emitted tokens count is still billable (we meter at the runtime boundary).
- Server-side interruption (Redwood fault/outage): for customer-impacting interruptions where the model or the runtime failed to complete an otherwise billable response, we proactively evaluate credits. Our standard approach is:
  * If outage is on our side and results in incomplete responses, we issue credits for the affected requests (we track request IDs and can reconcile).
  * For brief transient errors the runtime will attempt automatic resume/reconnects; duplicated tokens (retries that re-emit the same content) are detectable if requests are retried with the same client-generated idempotency key — in that case we avoid double-charging.
- Client-side retries: if the retry is initiated by the client with no idempotency key and results in a new request, it will be billed as a new request. We recommend using a lightweight client request id in metadata for deduplication.

Commercial notes:
- Baseline hosted API list price (public): 
  * prompt tokens: $0.0003 / 1k tokens
  * output tokens (streamed/generated): $0.0015 / 1k tokens
  These are example list numbers; your negotiated rate will depend on committed spend and usage profile.
- Streaming behavioral considerations: long-running sessions that keep a large KV cache active will also affect cost on the Dedicated plan vs Hosted. We can model explicit per-session memory if you need tighter caps.

Next steps: I can schedule a 30-min pricing call for this afternoon or tomorrow. If you want a commercial offer, Rishi (copied) can propose a discount ladder + one-time credit for early-month instability if you move to a reserved commitment.

Regards,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Adding a bit of commercial detail for procurement. Priya summarized the runtime behavior well; a few policy points we typically put into the SOW so expectations are explicit:

1) Exact billing triggers: tokens are counted at the runtime when they leave the model and are acknowledged by the serving layer. We do not retroactively bill for tokens that were generated but subsequently rolled-back by the runtime; however, tokens emitted before a client disconnect are captured.

2) Dedup / idempotency: we recommend a client-supplied request id header (x-client-request-id). If you reuse the same id for retries within a 2 minute window, our gateway will attempt deduplication and will not charge twice for the same emitted token set. This is reflected in our integration guide.

3) Outage credits: for measurable Redwood-caused interruptions that are reconciled to specific request ids, we issue pro-rated credits for the affected tokens. For commercial clarity we typically offer a one-time stability credit for new enterprise customers equivalent to 10k output tokens or a $500 credit (whichever is larger) covering the first 30 days post-launch — this is a standard concession we can include in the MAP if you pick a reserved commitment (minimum 6 months).

4) Edge cases & worst-case exposure: if clients repeatedly open/abandon streams at high QPS without idempotency keys, charges are real and can accumulate. We can add rate-limiting or per-session caps in your tenant to avoid runaway bills — that is a configuration we can include on Dedicated or as a managed setting on Hosted.

Suggested discount ladder for a committed hosted plan (examples):
- $0 - $50k / mo: list pricing (no discount)
- $50k - $200k / mo: 15% discount off list
- $200k+ / mo: 25%+ (tiered, negotiable depending on term)

If this looks good, Priya can pull together a short commercial offer and I’ll sign off on the credit line.

Rishi Malhotra
